title: Machine learning identifies the first enzyme for phenazine–thiol conjugation
summary: A genome-informed machine-learning workflow (ML-CITO) used contrastive learning over protein-language-model representations and genomic context, starting from 14 known phenazine-modifying sequences, to identify PTC. Biochemical characterization showed PTC catalyzes glutathione-dependent phenazine modification, a reaction previously assumed to occur non-enzymatically.
ai_technology: ML-CITO (genome-context-informed data augmentation plus protein-language-space contrastive learning)
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of California, Los Angeles; AITHYRA / Austrian Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A genome-informed machine-learning workflow (ML-CITO) used contrastive learning over protein-language-model representations and genomic context, starting from 14 known phenazine-modifying sequences, to identify PTC.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports that deleting the PTC gene did not cause a strong fitness disadvantage under tested conditions. The demonstrated chemistry and substrate context should not be generalized to other phenazine reactions.
evidence.ai_role: The model ranked candidate phenazine-interacting proteins from sparse known examples; the team then expressed and biochemically tested the candidate enzyme. AI nomination was a direct step in discovering the previously unknown enzymatic reaction.
